The *Migaṅgapañha* ("The Deer", Mil 7.5.7) is a section of the *Milindapañha* located in the seventh book of the collection [SuttaCentral]. Like neighboring chapters in this portion of the text, it employs a specific analogy—in this case, qualities associated with a deer (*miga*)—to illustrate spiritual practice and monastic qualities [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records that the text is connected with or mentions passages from canonical discourses, specifically the *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (MN 12; PTS MN i 68) and the *Sāriputtattheragāthā* (Thag 17.2) [SuttaCentral]. Three modern translations across three languages are cataloged on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

These correspondences consist predominantly of formulaic frames and structural parallels shared with other analogy sections (*aṅgapañha*) within the *Milindapañha*, such as the *Ākāsaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.6), *Āpaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.2), *Sūriyaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.4.8), *Meghaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.7.6), and *Māgavikaṅgapañha* (Mil 7.7.8) [DharmaNexus].
